claims.text: A 72-year-old woman was admitted with gradual onset of nonspecific visual changes. General physical examination was unremarkable and fundoscopic examination did not yield much. Conventional angiography revealed two aneurysms at the ophthalmic segment of the left internal carotid artery.

evidence.quote: A 72-year-old female
A 72-year-old female was admitted at our facility with gradual onset of nonspecific visual changes.
General physical examination was unremarkable.
Fundoscopic examination did not yield much.
Conventional angiography revealed 2 aneurysms at ophthalmic segment of the left ICA (Fig. 1A).

claims.text: Both aneurysms were treated with a pipeline embolization device without coils under general anesthesia. The device did not open well at the anterior curve of the siphon because the parent artery was tortuous, so a balloon was used to straighten it and implantation across both necks was achieved. Aspirin and clopidogrel were given after the procedure, and she was discharged on postoperative day 5 after repeated angiography detected no complications, with the aneurysm totally occluded before discharge.

evidence.quote: We treated both aneurysms with PLED (ev3/Covidien, Irvine, CA) without coils under general anesthesia.
Intraoperatively, the PLED did not open well at the anterior curve of the siphon (Fig. 1B) because the parent artery was tortuous
We achieved perfect implantation of the PLED across both aneurysmal necks’ after straightening the tortuous parent artery
we use HyperGlide5∗20 (Medtronic, Neurovascular, Irvine, CA) balloon to straighten the tortuous parent artery (Fig. 1C)
The patient was put on Aspirin 100 mg once daily and Clopidogrel 75 mg once daily after the procedure.
She was discharged home on postoperative day 5 after repeated conventional angiography detected no complications.
The aneurysm was totally occluded before discharge.

claims.text: Two months after the operation she was rushed to the emergency room with bilateral conjunctival congestion, and CT showed intracranial hemorrhage at the left temporal lobe. DSA established a left direct carotid cavernous fistula with multiple draining veins, and the rupture point was proximal to the pipeline device rather than the aneurysmal wall or sac.

evidence.quote: Two-month after the operation, the patient was rushed into the emergency room.
Physical examination revealed bilateral conjunctival congestion
emergency Computed tomography revealed intracranial hemorrhage at left temporal lobe

Digital subtraction angiography (DSA) established a left direct carotid cavernous fistula (CCF) with drainage via the bilateral superior ophthalmic veins, left superior and inferior petrosal sinuses, superficial middle cerebral vein, anterior cerebral vein and basal vein (Fig. 1E and F).
We also observed delayed spontaneous rupture of cavernous segment of the ICA following dual OSA treatment with PLED.
We detected that the rupture point was proximal to the PLED (Fig. 1G and H) and not the aneurysmal wall or sac.
(G and H) Are intraoperative DSA images showing the rupture point proximal to the PLED and not the aneurysmal wall or sac.

claims.text: The fistula was occluded with stent-assisted coils. Post-procedure DSA showed all draining veins eliminated except the inferior petrosal sinus, and she was discharged 2 weeks after the procedure with the hemorrhage absorbed. Two years of follow-up showed the patient well, with no neurological deficits and no recurrence of the fistula.

evidence.quote: Intraoperatively, we advanced enchelon-10 (Medtronic) into the fistula.
We used stent (Solitaire 6∗30) assisted coils to occlude the fistula.
On post procedure DSA, we observed that, the all the draining veins were eliminated except for the inferior petrosal sinus (Fig. 1I).
We discharged the patient 2 weeks after the procedure.
The intracranial hemorrhage was absorbed before discharge.
Two years follow-ups revealed that the patient is well with no neurological deficits and no recurrence of the fistula.

caption_claims.text:
Figure 1
(A) Is a conventional angiography showing 2 aneurysms located at ophthalmic segment of the left ICA. (B) Is intraoperative DSA showing inability of the PLED to open well at the anterior bend of the siphon because of the tortuosity of the parent artery. (C) Is an intraoperative showing straightening of tortuous of the parent artery with HyperGlide5∗20 (Medtronic) balloon. (D) Is a postoperative DSA showing perfect implantation of the PLED across both aneurysmal necks. (E and F) Are DSA images showing a left direct CCF with drainage from the bilateral superior ophthalmic veins, left superior and inferior petrosal sinuses, superficial middle cerebral vein, anterior cerebral vein, and basal vein. (G and H) Are intraoperative DSA images showing the rupture point proximal to the PLED and not the aneurysmal wall or sac. (I) Is a postoperative DSA, showing no draining veins except the inferior petrosal sinus. DSA = digital subtraction angiography, ICA = internal carotid artery, PLED = pipeline embolization device.
